name: CA-43
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a +27 partisan lean
Long-serving incumbent Maxine Waters running for re-election
Challenger Cristian Morales has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Waters near certain to win
model.rationale: Waters holds a seat with a +27 Democratic lean, has a large fundraising edge, and markets price her at roughly 95% to win; the challenger has shown no financial support. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A surprise surge of outside spending for Morales or unusually low turnout in the Democratic-heavy parts of the district could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maxine Waters seeks another term in a Los Angeles-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 27 points. She advanced to the general election as the incumbent and has raised more than $860,000, while challenger Cristian Morales reports no fundraising and has no visible outside support. Prediction markets put Waters' chances near 95 percent.

With no public polling and no expert ratings of the race, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, Waters' incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture. All signs point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than the outcome itself.
